thread.title: Tech Today: Amazon Trumped Again, Tesla Shootout, Buying Spotify

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Amazon Trumped Again, Tesla Shootout, Buying Spotify
text:
Here are some things going on today in your world of tech :
Spotify a Buy
Spotify ( SPOT ), the streaming music service that filed back in February for a direct listing on Nasdaq, starts trading next Tuesday, April 3 , and a couple of analysts are starting coverage in advance.
RBC Capital ’s Mark Mahaney this morning initiated coverage with an Outperform rating, and a $220 price target, writing that it is the "global leader” in a “very large global” market of $125 billion, and its “business model is inflicting up,” with its gross profit margin rising above 20% last year and showing a path to 30%-plus margin.
Also starting coverage is Atlantic Equities ’ James Cordwell , who starts the stock with an Overweight rating, and a $160 price target, writing the company is "well positioned to maintain its leadership position given its data advantage should enable it to offer a superior service."
Despite competition from Apple ’s ( AAPL ) Apple Music and others, Spotify's "richer music data and singular focus will enable it to offer the best service in terms of music discovery,” he writes.
Defending Amazon
Shares of Amazon.com ( AMZN ) are being squeezed by Trump pressure , falling $40.46, or almost 3%, at $1,390.96, after earlier falling by as much as 5%, this time because of a tweet from President Donald Trump himself, who recalled that he had warned before the 2016 election about Amazon’s skirting taxes and abusing the U.S. Postal Service .
This follows yesterday’s Axios piece about Trump being obsessed with the retail giant.
Defending Amazon this morning is Stifel Nicolaus ’s Scott Devitt , who follows up his note yesterday on the company with another one specifically rebutting the president. Writes Devitt, Trump is “wrong on taxes,” as Amazon would benefit from tax-law changes, while smaller retailers would be hurt. And he argues that Amazon has other options besides the Postal system.
Calming Words for Facebook
Another tech finding support today is Facebook ( FB ), rising $4.26, or almost 3%, at $157.29, for a second day in a row of gains. SunTrust Robinson Humphrey ’s Youssef Squali reiterates a Buy rating on the shares, and a $225 price target, writing that “the sell-off is overdone,” meaning, the 17% drop in the stock price since the revelation two weeks ago of Cambridge Analytica 's data mis-use.
“Digital advertisers we spoke to are not leaving FB,” observes Squali, "considering how effective the platform is relative to other channels,” and in addition, "we see no indication that users are fleeing FB en masse."
And Wedbush ’s Michael Pachter , who has an Outperform rating on the stock and a $260 price target, writes of having hosted a talk by the head of a digital marketing platform, who reaffirmed the unique advertising appeal of the platform. “Even if Facebook were to experience a negative impact on overall user growth,” writes Pachter, "our speaker believes that marketers would need to see meaningful declines within their specifically targeted cohorts before seriously re-evaluating their budget allocations."
Tesla Shootout
Shares of Tesla ( TSLA ) are down $6.26, or 2%, at $251.52, amidst a bit of a shootout over the stock this morning.
For the bull case , Instinet ’s Romit Shah reiterates a Buy rating, while cutting his price target to $420 from $500, writing that he’s “constructive on Tesla,” and that recent concerns about risk of insolvency are “largely without merit.” However, he does foresee a compression in stock multiples for large-cap tech, and he cuts his “Model 3” sedan estimates on “production constraints, and he anticipates a $3 billion capital raise” as soon as next quarter.
For the bear case , Brian Johnson with Barclays reiterates an Underweight rating, and a $210 price target, writing that the company is “behind in autonomous driving” compared to Alphabet ’s ( GOOGL ) Google’s Waymo unit, and that it’s “tough to make a case” about Tesla having “ancillary businesses” such as in energy .
Square’s Shift
Shares of Square ( SQ ) are up $1.46, or 3%, at $48.85, after Jefferies & Co. ’s Ramsey El-Assal this morning reiterated a Buy rating, writing that after a 15% pullback in the shares amidst tech’s sell-off, investors should pay attention to the company’s shift away from just payment fees.
"We come to the conclusion,” writes El-Assal, “that by 2022, SQ's Subscription & Services (S&S) will represent about half of adj. net revenues, which should prove nicely additive to valuation."
Fortinet’s Brighter Prospects
Shares of security technology vendor Fortinet ( FTNT ) are up 67 cents, or 1.3%, at $52.95, after BMO Capital ’s Keith Bachman this morning reiterated an Outperform rating on the shares, and raises his price target to $58 from $50, writing that the company can increase revenue from its products by “low-single digits” on a percentage basis, the next few years, better than what he had been expecting to date, namely flat sales.
"Additionally, we are raising our 2019 FCF estimate based on modest improvements in operating margins, steady cash cycle days, and lower capex,” writes Devitt.
Another Tech Index
Speaking of security, Piper Jaffray ’s Andrew Nowinski has issued his first-ever edition of what he calls the “Security, Storage and Networking Index,” tracking stocks across all three areas of tech, "to determine which of the three sub-segments investors should have the most exposure to."
He determines that while all three categories are collectively trading above the 5-year average for the group, storage is the most appealing.
“The Storage sector valuation looks much more favorable, as the sector is trading in line with the 5-year average EV/Revenue, but at a discount to the 5-year average EV/Free Cash Flow and P/E."
He recommends storage picks NetApp ( NTAP ) and Nutanix ( NTNX ).
Shares of NetApp and Nutanix are both slightly higher.
Hoping for ‘Cinematic VR'
The Washington Post’s Steven Zeitchik has a piece about " cinematic VR ” as the latest hope for the virtual reality industry, in particular the forthcoming Steven Spielberg -directed film, “Ready Player One,” which comes to theaters today.
The article Quote: s Walter parkes, co-chairman of Dreamscape Immersive, the company bringing a lot of cinematic VR to venues, as saying of the phenomenon, "Something is happening but we won’t know for two or three years or longer where it’s going to land."
Ready Player One had been mentioned earlier this month by Jefferies & Co . analyst Mark Lipacis as a potential catalyst for GPU chips from Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), as the chips are used to power VR in high-end computers.
